name: alpha-syn-mito-tnt-paper
title: α-Synuclein aggregates induce mitochondrial damage and trigger innate immunity to drive neuron–microglia communication
notes: Source: Nature Communications (2026) 17:6462, https://doi.org/10.1038/s41467-026-73136-7. Open access article; figures and text are reproduced here for agent retrieval.

Only the main article PDF was supplied. The Supplementary Information (Supplementary Figs. 1-12 and Supplementary Movies), the Reporting Summary, the Peer Review file, and the Source Data file cited by this article were not provided and are therefore absent from references/supplement.md.
Statements in the text that cite 'Supplementary Fig.' or 'Supplementary Movie' refer to that unsupplied material and cannot be checked against this package.

Figure links follow the article's print position, so a figure and its caption can sit under a later heading than the section that first cites them. The navigation index names the section where each figure is discussed; search 'Fig. N |' to jump to the caption itself.

sources.title: α-Synuclein aggregates induce mitochondrial damage and trigger innate immunity to drive neuron–microglia communication (Nature Communications, main article PDF)
sources.review_notes: All 21 pages of the main article PDF were inspected page by page against rendered previews and zoomed crops, by five reviewers over separate page ranges plus a coordinator pass. Checked: two-column reading order, heading hierarchy, figure crop completeness for Figures 1-9, verbatim figure captions including N/n values and p-values, Methods reagents with catalogue numbers and dilutions, the qRT-PCR primer table, and references 1-101 for sequence and completeness. The page-1 masthead was reclassified from a figure to an omission and the dates/authors/abstract block from a table to prose. Sentences split by the column and page layout were reconnected with join_previous, and a reading_order places each figure immediately before its own caption at a paragraph boundary. Printed defects in the article were kept verbatim rather than silently corrected.
